subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which adaptation helps a cactus survive in a hot desert?
options: Broad, flat leaves to catch rain
A thick, waxy stem to store water
questions.explain: A cactus stores water in its thick, waxy stem and has spines instead of leaves to reduce water loss.

questions.q: An advantage of solar power compared with coal is that it:
options: Produces no carbon dioxide when generating electricity
Is cheaper to run in every location
questions.explain: Solar panels generate electricity without burning fuel, producing no CO2 during operation, though output varies with sunshine.

questions.q: An animal that eats only plants is best described as a:
questions.explain: A herbivore is a primary consumer that feeds only on plants (producers).

questions.q: How are plants such as lianas and epiphytes adapted to life in the rainforest?
options: They climb or grow on other trees to reach sunlight
They store fat to survive droughts
They have thick fur to keep warm
They lose their leaves in winter
questions.explain: Lianas climb up tree trunks and epiphytes grow on branches, both reaching the light without making their own tall trunks.

questions.q: Compared with HICs, many LICs typically have:
options: No use of energy at all
questions.explain: People in lower-income countries generally consume far less energy per person than those in high-income countries.

questions.q: Why does the UK import a large share of its food?
options: Imported food is always cheaper to grow
The UK grows none of its own food
Demand for variety and out-of-season produce exceeds what the UK climate can grow
The UK has banned domestic farming
questions.explain: The UK imports food to meet year-round demand for variety and produce that its climate cannot grow, even though it produces much of its own.

questions.q: Which statement about food security is correct?
options: It means a country grows all its own food
It is the same as a food surplus
It only applies to wealthy countries
It means everyone has access to enough safe, nutritious food
questions.explain: Food security exists when all people have reliable access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food to meet their needs.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a water transfer scheme?
options: To move water from areas of surplus to areas of deficit
questions.explain: Water transfer schemes move water from regions with a surplus to regions with a deficit to balance supply and demand.

questions.q: Which human activity is a major threat to global biodiversity?
questions.explain: Destroying habitats removes the homes of plants and animals, reducing the variety of life (biodiversity).

questions.q: Which is the best example of sustainable water management?
options: Extracting groundwater faster than it refills
questions.explain: Cutting leaks and reusing grey water reduces demand and conserves supply, making them sustainable strategies.

questions.q: Which is a likely environmental impact of large-scale deforestation?
options: More carbon dioxide released and increased soil erosion
questions.explain: Cutting and burning trees releases stored carbon dioxide and exposes soil to erosion, while reducing biodiversity.

questions.q: What is the role of producers in a food chain?
options: They recycle nutrients into the soil
They convert sunlight into energy by photosynthesis
questions.explain: Producers such as green plants make their own food from sunlight through photosynthesis, forming the base of the food chain.

questions.q: What is the main job of decomposers in nutrient cycling?
options: They hunt and eat primary consumers
They produce energy from the Sun
They break down dead organisms and release nutrients into the soil
They prevent nutrients from entering the soil
questions.explain: Decomposers such as bacteria and fungi break down dead matter, returning nutrients to the soil for plants to reuse.

questions.q: Which is a non-renewable energy source?
questions.explain: Crude oil is a finite fossil fuel that cannot be replenished on a human timescale, unlike solar, geothermal and tidal energy.

questions.q: Which of the following is a leading cause of deforestation in the Amazon rainforest?
questions.explain: Cattle ranching, along with logging, mining and farming, is a major direct cause of Amazon deforestation.

questions.q: The UK's energy mix has changed in recent years by:
options: Increasing the share of renewables and gas while reducing coal
questions.explain: The UK has cut coal use sharply and increased the contribution of renewables (especially wind) and natural gas.

questions.q: Which of these is an opportunity provided by a hot desert environment?
questions.explain: The intense, reliable sunshine of hot deserts makes them ideal for generating solar power.

questions.q: Why is the soil in a tropical rainforest often surprisingly infertile?
options: Heavy rain leaches nutrients and most nutrients are stored in the vegetation
It is too cold for plants to grow
questions.explain: Most nutrients are held in the biomass; heavy rainfall quickly leaches the thin soil, so it is rapidly exhausted once trees are cleared.

questions.q: Why might a country face 'economic' water scarcity despite having water?
options: It has banned the use of water
It lacks the money or infrastructure to supply it
questions.explain: Economic water scarcity occurs where water exists but a lack of investment and infrastructure prevents people accessing it.

questions.q: A reservoir created by a dam is used to:
options: Store water and often generate hydroelectricity
questions.explain: Dams hold back water in reservoirs to provide a reliable supply and often to generate hydroelectric power.

questions.q: What does 'water security' mean?
options: Having more rivers than neighbouring countries
Reliable access to enough safe, affordable water
questions.explain: Water security is the reliable availability of an adequate, safe and affordable supply of water to meet a population's needs.

questions.q: Which of these best shows global inequality in food consumption?
options: Food is shared equally between all countries
Many people in HICs over-consume while millions in LICs are undernourished
Everyone eats roughly the same number of calories
LICs consume more calories per person than HICs
questions.explain: Food consumption is highly unequal, with over-consumption and obesity in many richer countries while undernutrition persists in poorer ones.
